subject: Cobalt Systems — post-call technical recap & POC plan
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Baker <tbaker@cobalt-systems.com>, ops-eng <ops@cobalt-systems.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + technical deep-dive — recap and proposed POC

Tom — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap while it’s fresh and proposed next steps for the POC. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Call summary (5/14):
- Pain: unpredictable 99th-percentile latency (spikes to ~900ms) on short prompts; occasional large KV-cache miss latency.
- Goal: end-to-end service-level target is 99th <= 300ms for user-facing short prompts (~<64 tokens).
- Throughput target: sustained ~6k inference RPS at peak for the internal scoring microservice (burst to 9k).
- Model constraints: want to evaluate open 70B-family model (quantized), need 2k–4k context window for some telemetry traces.
- Compliance/ops: Cobalt requires audit logs for inference calls (token counts, model version, route), and data residency in us-west region.

Initial technical notes / assumptions:
- We recommend a Dedicated pool for the POC (isolated GPUs + predictable latency) with multi-variant routing to fall back to a cheaper variant under load.
- KV cache tuning and prefix caching expected to reduce token cost and 99p latency — we'll run synthetic benchmarks to measure cache hit/miss effects.
- For throughput targets we’ll exercise continuous batching with small latency-aware buckets; we’ll parameterize batch windows in the POC.

Proposed POC plan & immediate asks (next 2 weeks):
1) POC kickoff — 60 minute tech kickoff with Cobalt eng + Redwood infra (please propose times).
2) Share the following from Cobalt: representative request distribution (sample traces), expected token length distribution, and any hard IP/data residency restrictions.
3) We’ll deliver: deploy matrix (attached), synthetic workload config, and an initial SLO monitoring dashboard.

Attachments included: cobalt-poc-deploy-matrix-v1.xlsx (deploy nodes / GPU config), kv-cache-latency-profiles.pdf (sample curves).

Next step from my side: I’ll coordinate availability for next Tue/Wed for the kickoff and Karthik will propose the initial synthetic benchmark parameters.

Cheers,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

Subject: Re: Intro + technical deep-dive — recap and proposed POC

Thanks for the concise recap, Jasmine — this matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 99th <= 300ms target is for the internal scoring service that feeds our UI, so end-to-end includes our network hops. The goal for the Redwood-hosted inference portion is 99th <= 200ms if achievable for short prompts.
- Token lengths: ~70% of requests < 40 tokens, 25% in 40–400 tokens due to context appended from user history, and ~5% long traces up to ~3k tokens (those can be routed to a different variant).
- Compliance: we can provide sample request logs (anonymized) and we need evidence that audit logs include model version, timestamp, and request id for each inference.

Availability: Tue 18 May 10:00–12:00 PDT works for our engs for the kickoff.

Also: can you outline what metrics Redwood will expose for the POC (latency percentiles, per-model token cost, cache hit rate, routing decisions)?

Best,
Tom
Head of Platform Engineering — Cobalt Systems
Tom.Baker@cobalt-systems.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 18:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + technical deep-dive — recap and proposed POC

Tom / team — quick technical reply on instrumentation and an initial POC config.

Instrumentation & exposed metrics (we’ll publish these to the POC dashboard):
- Latency: p50/p90/p95/p99 for generation-only and end-to-end (including queueing).
- Token metrics: tokens in/out per request, per-model token-cost estimate.
- Cache: KV cache hit rate, miss penalty distribution (ms), and prefix-cache effectiveness.
- Routing: per-request route decisions and fallback events, model variant served, and capacity-saturation signals.
- Ops: request id, model_version, node_id, region, and a truncated prompt hash for correlation (no raw prompt unless you opt in).

POC baseline compute topology (recommendation):
- Dedicated pool: 2 H100 nodes (4x H100 GPUs each) in us-west1 for the low-latency tier; 3x A100-backed nodes for the high-throughput batch tier.
- KV cache: colocated with the low-latency nodes; aggressive warmup during steady-state; measure 99p delta on miss.
- Batching config: latency-aware batch windows starting at 5ms, adaptive up to 25ms during bursts. We’ll tune for 99th <= 200ms generation time at short prompts.
- Models: evaluate two variants — (A) 70B quantized using Q4_K_M (lower mem, better throughput), (B) 70B fp16 for quality comparison. We’ll instrument a quality check on 200 representative prompts.

Synthetic benchmark plan we’ll run during POC kickoff: 
- Baseline: 10-minute ramp to 6k RPS with token distribution matching your sample.
- Stress: 5 x 1-minute bursts to 9k RPS to observe routing and fallbacks.
- Long-tail: 1% of requests with 2k+ tokens to validate memory/backpressure handling.

I’ve attached a deploy matrix and will share a short README explaining how to run the synthetic harness and ingest your sample traces. If you’re comfortable with the recommended GPU mix, we’ll provision the Dedicated pool for 3 days for an initial run.

--Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
